subject: Civil Engineering
title: Feasibility Studies
description: A quick, practical guide to Feasibility Studies.

hook.text: Before spending billions, someone must ask — is this project even possible and worth doing?

buildup.text: Feasibility studies evaluate technical, financial, environmental, and legal viability.

discovery.text: Cost-benefit analysis compares total project cost against expected returns over its lifetime.

twist.text: Many mega-projects pass feasibility on optimistic assumptions — then overrun by 50% or more.

climax.text: The Superconducting Super Collider passed feasibility but was cancelled at $2 billion — costs tripled.

punchline.text: Can we build it? Should we? Can we afford it? All three must be yes.

quiz.question: What does a feasibility study evaluate before a project begins?
options: Only the architectural aesthetics and design appeal
Technical, financial, environmental, and legal viability of the project
The number of workers available in the local labor market

details.summary: Feasibility studies evaluate whether a proposed construction project is viable by analyzing technical requirements, site conditions, regulatory constraints, market demand, financial projections, and environmental impacts.
details.whyItMatters: Feasibility studies prevent organizations from committing millions to projects that are technically impossible, financially unviable, or legally unpermittable, saving enormous sunk costs.
takeaways: Technical feasibility assesses whether the project can be physically built
Financial feasibility evaluates whether the project generates adequate returns
Environmental and regulatory feasibility identifies permitting obstacles early

faq.question: What is typically included in a construction feasibility study?
faq.answer: A feasibility study covers site analysis including soil and environmental conditions, preliminary design concepts, rough cost estimates, schedule projections, market analysis for revenue-generating projects, regulatory and permitting requirements, environmental impact assessment.

faq.question: How accurate are cost estimates at the feasibility stage?
faq.answer: Feasibility-level estimates are typically accurate to plus or minus 25 to 50%, reflecting the limited design information available. They are based on historical cost data from similar projects, area-based unit costs, and parametric models rather than detailed quantity takeoffs.
